quote: Due to the underlying subjectivity in the appreciation of the results, evaluations (one for recommendation, another for adaptation) are based on the opinion of human judges

We asked 24 Portuguese‑speaking volunteers to answer the surveys. Each survey was answered by four different judges, who scored the proverbs recommended for ten headlines, according to their relatedness and funniness.
we relied on human opinions. For this, proverbs were recommended by each method for each of the 60 headlines in the gathered set.
guideline: Judges scored expressions on relatedness (using scales like 'Not related' to 'Extremely related'), novelty (from 'I knew the expression well' to 'completely new'), and funniness (from 'Not funny' to 'very funny')
Judges were asked to rate (a) the relation between the proverb and the news title and (b) how funny the proverb is; later evaluations also included novelty.

Each survey was answered by four different judges, who scored the proverbs recommended for ten headlines, according to their relatedness and funniness, with the following questions: (a) 'How would you rate the relation between the proverbs and the news title?' [Not related (1); Remotely related (2); Considerably related (3); Extremely related (4)]; (b) 'In relation to the headline, how funny is each proverb?' [Not funny (1); Remotely funny (2); Considerably funny (3); Extremely funny (4)].
